source_item.title: U.S. 10-year yield briefly breaks 5% for first time since 2024 after Aug CPI

card.plain_headline: US 10-year Treasury yield tops 5% for first time in 2024
card.what_happened: The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note briefly surpassed 5%, a level not seen since 2024. This rise in yield, which moves inversely to bond prices, was triggered by recent inflation data (CPI) and expectations of continued higher interest rates.
card.what_happened_verbose: The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury bond, a key indicator of borrowing costs for the government and a benchmark for many other loan rates, briefly exceeded 5%. This is a significant psychological and technical level, and the last time it was breached was in 2024. The increase in yields is a direct response to higher-than-expected Consumer Price Index (CPI) data, which suggests inflation may be more persistent, and reinforces market bets that the Federal Reserve will need to keep interest rates elevated for longer, or even raise them further.
